title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Morning Brief – 18 November 2026
headline: Madras High Court Strikes Down Mineral Transport Ban as DVAC Registers Rs 1,427 Crore Sand Mining Case Against Former Minister Duraimurugan

sections.big_picture:
Tamil Nadu's political landscape faces intense legal and administrative scrutiny as the Madras High Court delivers a series of landmark judgments, including the striking down of Rule 3-A which restricted the inter-state transport of legally mined minerals. The judiciary's active posture also extends to local governance, education, and public safety, marked by stern directives against stray cattle menace and interventions in university leadership vacancies.

 Concurrently, the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has escalated its anti-corruption drive, registering a massive case involving former minister Duraimurugan and 16 officials over an alleged Rs 1,427 crore sand mining cartel. These developments intersect with shifting political alignments following Congress's exit from the DMK alliance, leading to notable diplomatic chilliness between former allies while opposition parties navigate controversies surrounding public demonstrations and digital commentary.

top_developments.headline: DVAC Files Corruption Case Against Former Minister Duraimurugan and 16 Officials Over Rs 1,427 Crore Sand Mining Cartel
top_developments.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a high-profile corruption case against senior DMK leader and former minister Duraimurugan alongside 16 government officials, implicating them in an alleged Rs 1,427 crore illegal sand mining scam. According to investigative findings released by the agency, the former minister allegedly conspired with private contractors to manipulate tender procedures and facilitate large-scale illegal mineral extraction across the state. Investigators state that the accused formed an entrenched cartel that systematically subverted state oversight mechanisms to siphon off public resources...

sections.government_and_administration: - **Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Inspects 108 Emergency Response Call Centre in Chennai:** Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay conducted an official inspection of the 108 Emergency Response Call Centre located within the Directorate of Medical and Rural Health Services premises in Teynampet, Chennai. Accompanied by senior health officials, the Chief Minister reviewed the operational readiness of emergency ambulances operated by EMRI GHS on behalf of the Tamil Nadu government. An official release detailed that the inspection focused on optimizing response times and upgrading medical equipment to handle critical public health emergencies across urban and rural districts. The governance initiative aims to reassure citizens regarding the reliability of state-sponsored emergency healthcare infrastructure while driving administrative efficiency within the health department. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/vijay-inspects-108-emergency-response-call-centre-in-chennai/article71711738.ece))
sections.political_parties_and_opposition: - **Stalin Avoids Rahul Gandhi's Call Amid Ongoing Alliance Realignment in Tamil Nadu:** Six months after the Congress party unilaterally exited the DMK-led alliance to align with the TVK-led administration, political tensions remain palpable in state politics. Reports indicate that national Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attempted to contact DMK president M.K. Stalin to extend an invitation for the launch of Sonia Gandhi's book, *Belonging*, in New Delhi. Sources close to the DMK leadership confirmed that Mr. Stalin deliberately avoided the telephone call to signal his continued displeasure over Congress's tactical shift. While the DMK chief formally greeted Sonia Gandhi regarding the publication, the personal snub underscores the deep-seated political friction and altered electoral calculus shaping Tamil Nadu's tripartite party dynamics. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/stalin-avoids-rahuls-phone-call-greets-sonia-on-her-book/article71713431.ece))
sections.assembly_courts_and_policy: - **Madras High Court Strikes Down Rule 3-A, Ruling Tamil Nadu Cannot Ban Inter-State Mineral Transport:** In a major victory for industrial associations and mining operators, the Madras High Court formally struck down Rule 3-A of the Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, which previously prohibited the transport of legally mined minerals to neighboring states like Karnataka and Kerala. The division bench ruled that the state government lacks the legislative competence to impose absolute bans on inter-state commerce of lawfully extracted minerals, noting that such restrictions infringe upon constitutional provisions regarding trade and commerce. Legal counsels for the petitioners argued that the blanket prohibition had crippled regional supply chains and caused severe financial losses to licensed quarry owners. The court's judgment mandates immediate administrative compliance, compelling state authorities to overhaul mineral transit regulations and re-issue permits without territorial discrimination. ([The News Minute](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxNU19kWkpiLUUxTno2bHJCQm1uY29CRlcteWt2QUlyQXZYYy1PU1ZRcF9hQkFHOFNHTHNOd0c1MkU5SW5VUlU3MzZkN0NMMUYwV0JlS0JmSnRSOGhyT0VjLTB2X2Vrd3phQjBUMkRGQUJrZlQwZWlRaEhCM1R2cm1yQWJ6dFRIZm5vZ3c0dUJBckh3WGRIVUxBTERnbWhJWVNjbjhyd282c09ubXFLdnRYZmtQS1pJNFFLYU9qZ3NB?oc=5))
sections.district_developments: - **Publishers Allege Policy Violations by DMK Government in Modern Library Book Procurements:** Independent publishing houses have raised serious allegations against the previous DMK administration, accusing authorities of violating their own 15-page book procurement policy during purchases for modern libraries in Madurai and Coimbatore. Introduced in 2024 to foster contemporary literature and modernize institutional libraries, the policy mandates strict transparency and objective selection criteria. Publishers claimed that officials bypassed established guidelines to favor specific literary works, prompting formal demands for immediate policy amendments to guarantee absolute accountability in future government acquisitions. Administrative spokespersons have yet to issue a detailed rebuttal regarding the alleged procedural lapses in the library procurement tenders. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/dmk-govt-vowed-own-policy-amend-guidelines-pubishers))
sections.what_to_watch_next: Observers should monitor upcoming proceedings in the Madras High Court regarding the NEET PG 2026 counselling stay and the Madurai Kamaraj University Vice-Chancellor vacancy hearings directed at Governor Arlekar. Additionally, political circles will closely track the legal fallout from the DVAC sand mining case against Duraimurugan and potential statewide reactions to the striking down of mineral transport bans over the next 24 to 48 hours.
